cards.title: Foreign Tax Credit (Form 1116)
cards.body: India TDS or tax on India-source income can often cut your US bill as a credit — not just a Schedule A deduction. Educational only, not tax advice.

detail.summary: If you are a US person taxed on the same income in India and the US, the Foreign Tax Credit (FTC) can reduce US tax by the qualifying foreign income tax you paid or accrued — usually better than deducting it. Claim it on Form 1116 (unless a small passive-only election applies). Educational only; not tax advice.

sections.heading: Who this helps
sections.body: Indian-origin US citizens and residents with India ties: bank/FD interest, dividends, mutual-fund distributions, rental income, or capital gains where India withheld tax (TDS) or you filed an India return. Also useful for dual-filing households comparing credit vs deduction each year.

sections.heading: Rough mechanics
sections.body: You generally choose credit or itemized deduction for qualified foreign income taxes. A credit reduces US tax liability dollar-for-dollar (subject to a limit); a deduction only reduces taxable income. The credit is limited to US tax on your foreign-source taxable income (figured on Form 1116). Unused credits can often carry back 1 year and forward 10. Small passive-only cases may elect to claim without Form 1116 if foreign tax ≤ $300 ($600 joint) and other IRS tests are met — that election kills carryovers for that year.

sections.heading: India–US angle
sections.body: Keep Form 16A / TDS certificates, India ITRs, and broker statements that show tax paid on India-source income. Not every India levy qualifies (must be an income / war-profits / excess-profits tax or a tax in lieu). Treaty interaction and separate limitation categories (e.g. passive vs general) matter — Pub 514 and the India–US income tax convention are the starting maps, not blogs.

sections.heading: Check-this action
sections.body: List 2025 India-source income lines and taxes paid/accrued. Open Form 1116 instructions and Pub 514; decide credit vs deduction before you file. If totals are tiny and only passive payee statements, check whether the no-Form-1116 election fits — otherwise plan Form 1116.

bullets: Credit usually beats deduction when you have US tax liability on that foreign income
Limit = roughly US tax × (foreign-source taxable income ÷ worldwide taxable income)
Keep India TDS proofs with your US return workpapers
Educational only — edge cases (PF, NRI status flips, contested tax) need a cross-border pro
steps: Gather India TDS certificates / tax paid proofs for the tax year
Separate income into Form 1116 categories (often passive vs general)
Skim IRS Pub 514 + Form 1116 instructions for limit and election rules
Choose credit vs deduction; attach Form 1116 unless the small-tax election clearly applies

sources.label: About Publication 514, Foreign Tax Credit for Individuals
IRS: Foreign Tax Credit – How to figure the credit

cards.title: Build F-You Money first
cards.body: Enough invested capital that a bad boss or a dumb deal cannot own your week. Freedom is the product; luxury is optional.
cards.source: The Simple Path to Wealth · JL Collins

detail.summary: JL Collins's F-You Money is a runway of invested savings that lets you choose work and spending on your terms. It is not flashy wealth; it is optionality.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: F-You Money is cash and investments large enough that you can walk from a toxic job, wait out a bad market for a house, or say no to a deal that violates your values. Paycheck dependency shrinks when the portfolio can cover months or years of living costs.

sections.heading: How Collins gets there
sections.body: Avoid high-interest consumer debt, raise the savings rate by living below your means, and put the surplus into low-cost broad index funds (he favors a simple total-stock approach like VTSAX). Stay invested through downturns; panic selling is how the path breaks.

sections.heading: Today's move
sections.body: You do not need full FIRE tonight. Aim for a concrete runway: estimate monthly spend, then track how many months your liquid + invested buffer already covers. Automate the next contribution so the buffer grows without willpower.

bullets: Freedom beats lifestyle inflation as the scoreboard
Savings rate is the throttle; index funds are the engine
Market noise is expected — the plan is to stay invested
steps: Write your real monthly burn (housing, food, transport, minimum debt)
Divide investable + emergency cash by that burn → months of runway
Automate one transfer this week into a low-cost total-market index fund or equivalent

cards.title: 1% better compounds
cards.body: Tiny daily upgrades beat heroic one-offs. Pick one habit you can finish in under two minutes.

detail.summary: James Clear's compounding idea: small improvements stack. The enemy is the all-or-nothing day that never starts.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body: If you get 1% better each day, the gains compound. If you wait for a perfect Monday plan, you often get zero days.

sections.heading: Two-minute rule
sections.body: Shrink the habit until it is too small to skip: open the book, put on shoes, write one sentence. Identity follows repetition.

bullets: Attach the habit to an existing cue (after coffee, after lunch)
Track a simple checkbox streak, not a perfect score
Never miss twice in a row
steps: Pick one habit under two minutes
Write the cue + place
Do it once today, then protect tomorrow's slot

cards.title: W-2 vs 1099 in one line
cards.body: W-2 means tax is withheld for you. 1099 usually means you set aside estimated tax yourself.

detail.summary: Misclassifying how you get paid is one of the fastest ways to get an April surprise.

sections.heading: W-2
sections.body: Employer withholds federal (and usually state) income tax plus Social Security and Medicare. Your paycheck already moved money to the IRS.

sections.heading: 1099 / contractor
sections.body: Payer generally does not withhold income tax. You are responsible for quarterly estimated taxes and self-employment tax planning.

sections.heading: Practical move
sections.body: If cash flow is mostly 1099, park ~25-30% of profit in a separate tax savings account until you refine the rate with a pro.

bullets: Keep invoices and mileage logs as you go
Quarterly estimates reduce underpayment penalties
State rules can differ from federal

cards.title: NotebookLM as a study desk
cards.body: Drop PDFs and get grounded answers with citations. Useful when you need a map before a long read.

detail.summary: NotebookLM works best as a document desk, not a free-floating chatbot. Grounding cuts hallucinations when sources are attached.

sections.heading: Best use
sections.body: Upload a small set of related PDFs or notes, ask for an outline, contradictions, and glossary before you deep-read.

sections.heading: Trust rule
sections.body: Treat answers as a map. Click citations and verify the paragraph before you act on money, legal, or medical claims.

bullets: One notebook per project beats a junk drawer
Ask for bullet summaries with page pointers
Export notes you want to keep outside the chat
steps: Create a notebook for one topic
Upload 2-5 source files
Ask for outline + open questions
Verify two citations by hand

cards.title: Bedrock Guardrails first
cards.body: Put content filters and topic blocks on the model path before you stack agents.

detail.summary: Guardrails are cheaper than incident review. Wire them early on shared accounts and demos.

sections.heading: Why first
sections.body: Prompt-only safety instructions drift. Guardrails apply consistently across models and apps in the account.

sections.heading: What to configure
sections.body: Content filters for hate/insults/sexual/violence/misconduct, denied topics for your domain, and optional word/PII filters.

sections.heading: Ops tip
sections.body: Log interventions. If guardrails fire constantly, your product prompt or retrieval is the bug, not the filter.

bullets: Attach the same guardrail ARN in every env
Test with red-team prompts before launch
Prefer deny-by-default on sensitive topics

cards.title: SSD deal checklist
cards.body: Match capacity, warranty, and DRAM vs DRAMless. Cheap that dies mid-project is not a deal.

detail.summary: Storage deals hide tradeoffs in firmware, DRAM, and endurance. Buy for the workload, not the splashy GB price.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body: Confirm interface (NVMe Gen3/Gen4), usable capacity after formatting, warranty years, and TBW endurance if you write heavily.

sections.heading: DRAM vs DRAMless
sections.body: DRAM-less drives can be fine for light laptop use. Heavy compile/VM/database work usually prefers DRAM-backed models.

sections.heading: Red flags
sections.body: No brand warranty page, recycled listing photos only, or prices far below street for the same SKU.

bullets: Prefer sellers with clear return windows
Clone and verify before wiping the old drive
Leave 10-20% free space for SSD health
steps: List your must-have capacity + interface
Compare TBW and warranty on two finalists
Buy only if return policy is clear

cards.title: Short push day
cards.body: Incline push-ups, dumbbell press, lateral raises, overhead extension. Three hard sets each.

detail.summary: A compact push session when time is short. Quality reps beat random burnout.

sections.heading: Session
sections.body: Incline push-up 3x8-12, dumbbell bench press 3x8-12, lateral raise 3x12, overhead triceps extension 3x10-12.

sections.heading: Effort
sections.body: Stop with about one rep in reserve. Rest ~75-90s on compounds and ~60-75s on isolation.

bullets: Warm up shoulders with arm circles and empty-hand presses
Keep ribs down on overhead work
Log the top set weight for next time
steps: Warm-up 3 minutes
Run the four lifts
Optional finisher: close-grip push-ups to near failure

cards.title: Protect a deep block
cards.body: Schedule one 90-minute focus block with the phone in another room.

detail.summary: Shallow work expands to fill the calendar. Deep work needs a fence, not wishful multitasking.

sections.heading: The rule
sections.body: One protected block beats eight fragmented attempts. Put it on the calendar like a meeting with someone you respect.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.body: Phone elsewhere, notifications off, single document or IDE focused. Start with a written finish line for the block.

bullets: Same time of day builds a cue
Start with 50-90 minutes, not a heroic half day
End by writing the next block's first step
steps: Pick tomorrow's deep block time
Define the output in one sentence
Remove the phone before you sit down

cards.title: Standard deduction reality check
cards.body: Most filers take the standard deduction. Itemizing only wins above that floor.

detail.summary: Do not assume itemizing is virtuous. Math first, paperwork second.

sections.heading: Standard deduction
sections.body: A fixed amount based on filing status. If your eligible itemized expenses are below it, the standard route usually wins.

sections.heading: When itemizing can win
sections.body: Large mortgage interest, big charitable gifts, high state/local taxes (subject to caps), or major medical expenses above thresholds.

sections.heading: Habit
sections.body: Keep receipts anyway. Year-end is a bad time to reconstruct donations and medical costs.

bullets: Check the current-year IRS standard deduction table
SALT deduction caps matter for many households
Software comparisons are fine; verify weird results
